frames.narration: The provider sends a webhook: id=evt77, order 1001, amount 500. It adds a tag computed with a key that only the provider and the shop know.
The tags match, so the body was not changed and a holder of the key sent it. The shop credits the order once.

The attacker, who can post to the public endpoint, changes the amount to 9999 and hashes the new body. With only a plain hash the shop could not tell. With HMAC the attacker has no key, so the tag is wrong and the request is rejected.

Now the trap. Suppose the provider had used hash(secret + body) as its tag. The attacker sees one valid tag, appends &amount=9999 and keeps hashing from that tag (with a real hash such as SHA-256 the original padding bytes would sit in between; the toy hash has no padding). The shop recomputes hash(secret + longer body) and it matches.
HMAC closes it: the outer hash hides the inner state, so there is nothing to continue from. The same extension attempt on an HMAC tag fails.
The attacker has captured the exact request and sends it again 10 seconds later. The tag is valid, so a shop that only checks the signature credits the order a second time.

Defence: the shop checks that the signed timestamp is recent and asks the store whether evt77 was already processed. It was, so the replay is dropped. Anything older than the window is rejected by the timestamp alone.
